Such storms are mostly restricted to the coastal plains areas (Landers, 1970). Tornadoes are rare in the Appalachian Mountains (United States Weather Bureau, 1960). During the period 1916 to 1950, a total of 106 tornadoes occurred in South Carolina, and 62 in North Carolina. During this period, about 88 tornadoes occurred within a radius of approximately 100 miles of the Bad Creek site (this area including portions of North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Georgia) (United States Weather Bureau, 1960). The Applicant states that a total of 40 tornadoes occurred in a 2 degree square (about 125 miles by 125 miles) over the site area during the period of 1916 to 1955, for a recurrence interval at the site itself of 5,525 years.
2.4.2 Air and Noise Monitoring
2.4.2.1 Air Quality
Air quality meas rements are made by the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control, Bureau of Air Quality Control, which has the responsibility for defining the air quality of the State of South Carolina. Air quality is indexed by measurements taken at the Pickens County Health Department, Pickens, South Carolina, situated about 17 miles southeast of the Bad Creek site.
The sampling station classification was center city, commercial. Table 2-20 shows the results of sampling during 1972-1974. Table 2-21 shows the ambient air quality standards for the State of South Carolina.
It is probable that general air quality would exceed that of the Pickens sampling station in purity due to the mountainous, undeveloped nature of the project site.
